title: The Other
text:
He invented himself a face.
+
+Behind it
+
+he lived, died, and rose again
+
+many times.
+
+His face
+
+today bears that face’s wrinkles.
+
+His wrinkles have no face.
editorial_note: The repetitions of face and wrinkles remain unsmoothed, allowing persona, aging, and facelessness to undo one another line by line.

title: My Hands…
text:
My hands
+
+open the curtains of your being
+
+dress you in another nakedness
+
+uncover the bodies of your body
+
+My hands
+
+invent another body for your body.
editorial_note: The erotic paradox of dressing the beloved in nakedness is preserved, as is the repeated body through which touch discovers and invents.

title: With Eyes Closed
text:
With eyes closed
+
+you light yourself from within
+
+you are the blind stone
+
+Night after night I carve you
+
+with eyes closed
+
+you are the open stone
+
+
+We become immense
+
+only by knowing each other
+
+with eyes closed
editorial_note: Franca is rendered as open, answering the earlier blind stone through availability rather than eyesight; carving and mutual knowledge occur without external vision.

title: The Poet’s Fate
text:
Words? Yes, made of air,
+and lost in air.
+
+
+Let me lose myself among words,
+let me be the air upon a pair of lips,
+a wandering breath without contours
+that air dissolves.
+
+
+Light too loses itself within itself.
editorial_note: Air is simultaneously the poem’s substance, passage, and erasure; the final light repeats that self-loss without being made into consolation.

title: Words? Yes, Made of Air…
text:
Words? Yes, made of air,
+
+and lost in air.
+
+
+Let me lose myself among words,
+
+let me be the air upon a pair of lips,
+
+a wandering breath without contours
+
+that air dissolves.
+
+
+Light too loses itself within itself.
editorial_note: This separately sourced witness of “The Poet’s Fate” keeps the same reviewed wording while preserving its more widely spaced lineation.

title: Salvos
text:
Tower of amber walls,
+solitary laurel in a stone plaza,
+an unforeseen gulf,
+a smile in a dark corridor,
+the gait of a river flowing between palaces,
+sweet comet that blinds me and recedes…
+
+
+Bridge beneath whose arches life forever runs.
editorial_note: Salvas is retained as the multivalent Salvos—salutes, bursts, and acts of saving—while the sequence of metaphoric glimpses flows into the final bridge.

text:

+

editorial_note: This distinct lineated witness of “Salvos” preserves the reviewed metaphoric sequence and its expanded pauses.

title: With a Piece of Charcoal…
text:
With a piece of charcoal
+
+with my broken chalk and my red pencil
+
+to draw your name
+
+the name of your mouth
+
+the sign of your legs
+
+upon nobody’s wall
+
+
+Upon the forbidden door
+
+to carve the name of your body
+
+until the blade of my knife
+
+bleeds
+
+and the stone cries out
+
+and the wall breathes like a chest
editorial_note: The infinitives retain the poem’s incantatory incompletion; inscription passes from charcoal and chalk to a blade until inert surfaces acquire blood, voice, and breath.
